I used to be wrong, now I'm right.

I've become far more open to different ideas since I've gotten older.

When I was a young punk, I hung out in socialist activist circles, bemoaning how stupid adults were to elect somebody like Reagan. We needed a revolution, I thought back then. The solutions seemed so simple. Tax the rich and give to the poor. I imagine if I was the same kind of person back then I would be a big Bernie Sander supporter. I also would have been insufferable on Tumbler or whatever other social media the kids are into.

As I started hitchiking in my early twenties, I found myself exposed to people from all walk of life. All sort of different ways of looking at the world. Turns out those "evil" conservatives weren't so bad after all.

By the time I hit thirty I was a pretty mainstream Democrat, working in the midst of the dot com boom. I supported Clinton. I did find my votes for congress about evenly split, depending on the issues I cared about.

By forty I was more conservative. There were some systemic problems that were made worse by regulations, and the expansion of the state. I was also alarmed by the level of military intervention seen in the 90s. Nation building was never something our military, or any military, was built for. I had hoped that by voting Republican we might see less of that sort of thing. (9/11 was a game changer on that).

At 50? I've pretty much given up on all of it. It's not my world any more, and it's time to hand the torch of to people who give a damn. Team red or team blue are exactly the same. As a whole, this country agrees on pretty much 95% of the issues...we only disagree on the means of achieving them. The things we get worked up about, and angry at each other over, will seem as abstract and pointless as the 19th century debates over tariffs do to us today.

Younger readers, I hand it all over to you. I'll be sitting on my porch yelling at the tax man, but I'm out. May not even vote this time around.

As I've gotten older and made myself a little bit of money, I realize that it's difficult to help everyone. I think that's what people realize... Everyone needs help, until you realize how difficult it is to become successful yourself, then you want to stay that way. I still volunteer, donate to charity, etc... But like /u/NeedleStack said, it's almost a 180 from college know-it-all days.

Not only is it impossible to help everyone, it's difficult to create lasting change, or even do more good than harm. For example, giving money to a needy person might prevent them from helping themselves get out of poverty by keeping them dependent. Foreign aid can cause harm -- often a large amount of food is given to some African country. This lowers the prices of food and farmers in Africa can't compete with free food -- they go out of business. Next year not enough food is grown. Now the country really needs food.

It's difficult to help people.
